items.title: George Benson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Johnny Smith – Johnny “Hammond” Smith – was a great organist too.

ctx.x: Great lesson for you youngsters. If we return to the chronology, the next recording that’s listed here is Brother Jack McDuff Quartet with Benny Golson Big Band. Do you recall that?
Jack’s hero was the great Jimmy Smith, of course. He respected other players. Johnny Smith – Johnny “Hammond” Smith – was a great organist too. But Jimmy was

his favorite. He was flashy and always bluesy and funky, and he had these fabulous records, Walk on the Wild Side with Oliver Nelson. Jack wanted to do something similar. So they hired Benny Golson, who’s a great arranger himself and a great musician too. But he used me on the record. I said, oh man. You know, I don’t read any music, see? They had all this music. I said, uh oh. Here it comes. I’m looking at all this music. I said, man, they got some notation. [Benson sings a melody.] I said, oh no. But they made…
